Title: Virginia to hold referendum on redistricting plan

Summary: 
Virginia is set to hold a voter referendum on a redistricting amendment passed by its legislature, following a special session in October 2025 and a 62-33 vote in the House earlier this week, with the Senate approving it on Friday. The measure, if approved in the referendum, would allow Democrats to redraw the state's congressional map earlier than usual, potentially shifting representation from the current 6-5 Democratic advantage to a projected 10-1 Democratic dominance, according to House Speaker Don Scott and Senate President pro Tempore L. The move is framed by Democrats as a necessary response to Republican-led gerrymandering efforts in states like Texas, Missouri, and North Carolina, which were driven by former President Donald Trump. Democratic Senate Majority Leader Scott Surovell condemned Trump as a 'hyper-partisan, fascist ideologue' seeking to manipulate state legislatures for personal political gain. Republican state Sen. The current map is nearly balanced, with Democrats holding six seats and Republicans five. The referendum is expected to pass, though reactions remain sharply divided along partisan lines. The development marks a significant Democratic strategic move ahead of the 2026 midterm elections in the broader national gerrymandering contest that began in August 2025 when Texas unveiled a map reducing Democratic representation by five seats.

Myers cautioned that even if the referendum is allowed, its passage is uncertain due to voter awareness and turnout challenges, and if passed, the new map would significantly disadvantage Republicans by creating heavily Democratic-leaning districts.
